clue.text: Covering report

definitions.meaning: the protective outer layer of a tree trunk
the sharp explosive sound of a gun firing

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a tree's outer skin, and the crack a gun gives when fired, both called by the same word.

clue.text: Keep playing or stick?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, to carry on batting is to ...
a short rod, such as a conductor's or a relay runner's

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is the cricket phrase for carrying on batting; read as one, it is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A relay runner or conductor holds this short rod, an ordinary example of a stick.

clue.text: Progressively move heart of British comic writer

indicators.note: the heart is what is left when the outermost letters at each end of the writer's surname are trimmed off

parts.note: Terry Pratchett, British author of the comic Discworld fantasy novels

explanation.surface: Someone tries to shift the emotional core of a much-loved British humorist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' strips P and T from the ends of PRATCHETT; the writer is never named, so this is a deletion from a synonym, not letters printed in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To ratchet something up or down is to shift it step by step, as a toothed mechanism does.

clue.text: Foresight of French when invading local territory

indicators.note: invading means pushing into the middle of the territory, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a province is a regional territory of a country
de is the French word for of

explanation.surface: A historical note on French foresight shown when an army invaded a neighbouring region.
explanation.definitionFit: An older sense of the word is prudent forethought, careful planning for the future.

clue.text: Wealthy doctor keeping on in part of London

parts.note: wealthy means rich

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the doctor's letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: MD, Doctor of Medicine

explanation.surface: A rich physician hangs on to a property in a smart district of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Richmond is a leafy borough in south-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Richmond is a borough and district on the Thames in south-west London, so an example of an area of the city.

clue.text: Harshness deposing pair of leaders, it's true

definitions.note: a definition by description: a statement that is true, a truth

indicators.note: deposing means removing from the top, and a pair of leaders are the first two letters of the word

parts.note: harshness means severity

explanation.surface: Political comment: a harsh regime overthrows two leaders, and that is the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposing pair of leaders' takes SE off the front of SEVERITY.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a truth or a principle accepted as true, so 'it's true' describes one.

clue.text: Duke finished port

parts.note: finished means over, as in 'the game is over'

explanation.surface: A nobleman is done for in a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover is the English Channel port in Kent closest to France, a ferry harbour.

clue.text: Irishman around pub picked up nurses

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking something up lifts it so the letters read from bottom to top
around means the Irishman's name surrounds the pub

parts.note: Sean is a common Irish man's name
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: An Irish drinker hangs around the bar and is collected by nurses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns SEINNAN upward, as a down entry reads.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are verbs for looking after someone carefully, as a nanny does a child.

clue.text: Lady's year ruined — back in January, it would seem?

definitions.text: back in January, it would seem?
definitions.note: a playful description: January is when the year is young

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of the two words are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A woman's year has been wrecked, and she looks back to how it started in January.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a time too soon to judge, and literally January sits at the start of the calendar.

clue.text: German leader's encouragement to repeat company's initial investing in German currency

parts.note: bis is a call from an audience for a piece to be played again, an encore

indicators.note: investing means putting something into, so the initial goes inside the currency

parts.note: the mark was Germany's currency before the euro

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A financial tip: repeat the firm's first move of putting money into German currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initial' takes C from company's; 'investing in' puts it inside MARK.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto von Bismarck was the first chancellor of the united German Empire, so a historical head of state.

clue.text: Unison passage? Annoyed comment before it's played back

parts.note: tut is the click of the tongue expressing irritation

indicators.note: played back, like a recording rewound, means the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A musician tuts at a passage in unison before the recording is replayed.
explanation.definitionFit: In a score the instruction tutti marks a section where all the players perform together.

clue.text: Camel-rider, perhaps, caught by a pair of Arabs carrying blade

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the doubled letters enclose the blade
a pair means two copies of the abbreviation

parts.note: Ar is the abbreviation for Arab or Arabic
a vane is a blade, as on a windmill or propeller

explanation.surface: A camel rider is captured by two Arabs who are carrying a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller in a desert caravan might well be riding a camel, so this is an example, signalled by 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Prophet repelled an intrusive smell

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the little word is turned around

parts.note: a hum is slang for an unpleasant, pervading smell

explanation.surface: A holy man is driven away by a smell that won't leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Nahum is one of the minor prophets with a book in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Obstetric study? Degree takes a long time, though not at first

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter of the word is left off

parts.note: an eternity is a very long time, informally

explanation.surface: A degree in obstetrics takes ages to finish, though not at the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not at first' drops the E from ETERNITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstetrics deals with pregnancy and childbirth, the subject of a maternity ward.

clue.text: American backing computer pioneer for surgical procedure

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: US, the United States
Alan Turing, British pioneer of computer science

explanation.surface: An American supports a famous computer scientist's work towards a surgical operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitching a wound closed is a standard operation in surgery.

clue.text: Dreadful input, alas, for letter writer

indicators.note: dreadful means awful, so the letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone groans at the awful material fed in by a correspondent.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle wrote the epistles of the New Testament, letters to early churches.

clue.text: English discernible in handwriting leading to a celebration

indicators.note: discernible in means seen inside, so the letter sits within the other word

parts.note: fist is informal for a person's handwriting

explanation.surface: Englishness shows in someone's handwriting, which leads to a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festive holiday or party, particularly in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Each city developed winter sports racer?

indicators.note: developed means changed and built up, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Every town has built up a racer for winter sport.
explanation.definitionFit: This sailing craft runs on runners over frozen lakes, and is raced in winter.

clue.text: Wet smear spoiled glasses

indicators.note: spoiled means ruined, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A damp smudge has marred the glassware.
explanation.definitionFit: Stemware is the collective name for drinking vessels with stems, such as wine goblets.

clue.text: Wrote mostly about expression of gratitude for new pupils

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened word goes round the thanks
mostly means most of the word, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: inked means wrote in ink
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A teacher wrote much of a thank-you note for the newcomers.
explanation.definitionFit: A school's intake is the batch of pupils enrolled at one time, its new arrivals.

clue.text: Oath's half covered by loud noise

indicators.note: half here means the second half of the word for a sworn promise

parts.note: under means covered by, as in 'under a blanket'

explanation.surface: Half of someone's swearing is drowned out by a din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes TH, the back half of OATH.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunder is the rumbling crash after lightning, and by extension any loud booming sound.

clue.text: Tries US lawyers, bringing in hired staff member?

indicators.note: bringing in means taking someone inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: atts is short for attorneys, American lawyers
a temp is a temporary worker hired through an agency

explanation.surface: American lawyers prosecute cases with help from a temporary office worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are plural nouns or verbs for efforts made to do something.

clue.text: Setter's cross about one peculiar bird

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the setter's letters go round the jumbled number

parts.note: Phi is the setter of this puzzle
X is the shape of a cross

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: The puzzle's author is annoyed at one strange bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Phi set this puzzle, so 'Setter's' is his pen-name; 'peculiar' gives OEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The phoenix is the mythical bird said to be reborn from its own ashes.

clue.text: Midsummer lover, he left one from Scotland upset

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in this down entry the Scottish word is reversed

parts.note: ane is the Scots word for one

explanation.surface: A summer romance ends: he walks out, and the Scottish girl is distraught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ANE into ENA. Helena chases Demetrius in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: In A Midsummer Night's Dream Helena is one of the four young lovers in the woods.

clue.text: Strengthened support? Same burst in earthquake

indicators.note: an earthquake shakes everything up, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: The same thing burst apart during a tremor, despite reinforcement.
explanation.definitionFit: This beam is braced by a frame of struts, making a reinforced structural member.

clue.text: Pitiless on being confined in pen

indicators.note: being confined in means shut up inside, so the small word is enclosed

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: Someone shut away in a pen without mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: A stony stare or heart is hard and unfeeling, showing no mercy.

clue.text: Love a story not involving rugby?

indicators.note: not involving means leaving out, so the letters for the sport are dropped

parts.note: a rumour is a story going around
RU is the abbreviation for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: A romance whose tale has nothing to do with the rugby club.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is a love affair, borrowed from the French word for love.

clue.text: Scoundrel's good shifting cosmetic

indicators.note: shifting means moving to a new place within the same word

parts.note: a scoundrel is a rogue; the 's is 'has'

explanation.surface: A villain's virtue has moved over into make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' moves the G of ROGUE one place along.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouge is red powder or cream applied to colour the cheeks, a make-up product.

clue.text: Classical princess and classic city advertisement recalled

parts.note: Rome, the city of classical antiquity

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: A mythical princess, an ancient city and a withdrawn advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Andromeda was the Ethiopian princess chained to a rock and rescued by Perseus.

clue.text: Only one component of skean-dhu will do for Indian?

definitions.text: Only one component of skean-dhu will do for Indian?

parts.words: Only one component of skean-dhu will do for Indian?
parts.note: only the second part of the Scottish dagger's name, with its 'doo' sound, serves to end the word for an Indian of a particular faith

explanation.walkthrough: A skean-dhu is the small knife worn in a Highland stocking; its 'dhu', said 'doo', supplies the ending sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Most people in India follow the religion whose followers are called this, so it names an Indian.

clue.text: Lacks ready cooked sweet treats

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or fiddled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A baker short of anything ready to eat whips up some cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges LACKSREADY. Lardy cakes are rich English fruit buns made with lard.
explanation.definitionFit: These rich spiced fruit buns from southern England are a sweet baked teatime treat.

clue.text: Car part cut after length installed

indicators.note: installed means fitted inside, so the letter is put within the other word

parts.note: to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: A mechanic cuts a component after fitting it to a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The rod on which a vehicle's wheels turn is a key piece of a car.
